HSN.AX.answer:
Hansen (HSN.AX) is down about 30% year to date, to A$3.58. It's down about 36% over 12 months. The chart above shows the slide, and its biggest single-day drop came on Aug 19.

**The size of the fall:** From its 52-week high of A$5.81 (Nov 26, 2025), the stock fell 48.7% to a low of A$2.98 on Sep 28, 2026. The S&P/ASX 200 rose 0.8% over the same dates, so this was company-specific, not a market move. It has since bounced about 20% off that low and is still 38% below the high.

**What drove it:**
- **August results and a leadership change** (Aug 19, -21.2% to A$3.30 on about 25x normal volume): This was the biggest single hit. Kalkine reported the shares slid about 19% as revenue fell 1.5%, even though profit and cash flow were higher. On the same day the company named Stuart MacDonald as the new CEO, with founder Andrew Hansen moving to Executive Chair, according to The Motley Fool Australia. A Reuters-sourced headline the day before said Hansen expects revenue growth in FY28. Simply Wall St described the setup as a "transition year" after margin strength. It also noted the stock was already down about 31% over three months going into the result. My read is that a revenue decline, a CEO handover and growth pushed out to FY28 were more than the market would accept, even with better profit.
- **Earlier weakness, Feb 2026** (Feb 4 -6.3%, Feb 6 -5.7%, Feb 24 -5.6%, with Feb 4 and Feb 6 on about 2.3–2.5x normal volume): The news available doesn't reach back to those dates, so I can't say what caused them. The stock did jump 16% on Feb 18 on 6x volume, so the first half of the year was choppy.
- **Sep 18** (-5.6% on 3x volume): No reported catalyst turned up for it. The stock hit its low ten days later.

**Since then:** Recent news is mostly positive but minor, including Hansen supporting new Vodafone UK mobile offerings and an industry award. There's also a director departure notice (David Trude, Nov 19). Shaw and Partners called the stock deeply undervalued and tipped it to double within 12 months, but that is the broker's view, not mine.

The stock is trading as a turnaround story, so the next things to watch are whether revenue returns to growth and how the new CEO executes.

HOOD.answer:
**Robinhood (HOOD) is down about 32% in four weeks, from $101.93 on Oct 21 to $69.17 on Nov 18.** The S&P 500 fell 5.6% over the same dates, and the financials sector ETF (XLF) rose 0.7%. So this is mostly a Robinhood and crypto-linked selloff, not a market or sector move. The stock is now about 50% below its Dec 2025 high of $137.08 and just above its 52-week low of $65.16. As the chart shows, the slide came in steps rather than one crash. Today it was flat (-0.03%).

**What drove it**
- **Crypto slide and election fallout** (Nov 5, -10.3% on 1.6x normal volume): this was the biggest day. Benzinga reported HOOD plunged as Bitcoin dipped after the midterms. Yahoo Finance reported that fintechs SoFi and Affirm also fell hard, because investors worried a Democratic Congress could weigh on the sector. Crypto is a big swing factor for Robinhood, and Traders Union said on Nov 18 that HOOD was "holding near lows" amid crypto headwinds.
- **A Q3 report that didn't thrill** (reported Oct 27 after the close): revenue was a record $1.42B, up 12%. But EPS fell 16% to $0.51 and adjusted EPS fell 3%. Crypto revenue dropped 55% to $120M, and net interest revenue fell 9%. Event contracts (prediction markets) grew more than 6x to $173M, and options and equities were strong. The Motley Fool said the results "didn't thrill investors." Earnings were also hit by $67M of unrealized losses on Robinhood's own venture fund. The following sessions, including Oct 30 (-7.2%), were weak.
- **Prediction-market risk**: the news mentions "Kalshi risk" and Variational raising $110M to compete with Robinhood and Interactive Brokers (Finance Magnates). Prediction markets are now a major growth leg, so any competition or regulatory worry matters more.
- **Insider selling**: this looks minor. A director's trust filed two Form 144 notices of intended sales, about $5M each, on Oct 21 and Nov 17. Form 4s show about $9.9M of completed sales in the window. These are small next to the size of the drop.

**Gaps in the evidence**
- Oct 22 (-5.3%), Oct 30 (-7.2%) and Nov 16 (-7.5%) have no clearly attributable article in the news I could pull. I won't guess at a cause. The most likely common thread is the crypto and fintech pressure above, but that's inference.
- The 5-day drop is -18%, so the latest leg down is the sharpest part of the slide.

**What's next**
- Analysts remain bullish. Mizuho reportedly sees about 86% upside, though that's the Street's view, not mine.
- The business is still growing: record revenue, record Gold subscribers (5.2M), and $16B of net deposits in Q3. The selloff is more about multiple compression and crypto sensitivity than a collapse in the business.

Want me to build the full DCF and report to see whether $69 is below fair value? I can also pull the technicals, since the stock is near its March low.

MENLO PARK, Calif. – October 27, 2026 – Robinhood Markets, Inc. (“Robinhood”) (NASDAQ: HOOD) today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2026, which ended September 30, 2026.
"Our vision is to make everyone an owner, because broad ownership is essential to a free, stable, and prosperous society," said Vlad Tenev, Chairman and CEO of Robinhood.
"Customers are trusting us with more of their assets as we deliver on our product roadmap, leading to our highest quarter ever for revenues," said Shiv Verma, Chief Financial Officer of Robinhood. "We also added a new business cylinder with over $100 million in annualized revenues this quarter as Rothera scaled rapidly. And we're entering Q4 with strong momentum, as October Net Deposits have already topped $13 billion month-to-date, including $6 billion from the Dell family's contribution to Trump Accounts."
Third Quarter Results
• Total net revenue s increased 12% y ear-over-year to $1.42 billion.
◦ Transaction-based revenues increased 19% year-over-year to $867 million , primarily driven by event contracts revenue of $173 million, up over 6x , op tions revenue of $399 million , up 31%, and equities revenue o f $121 million, up 41%, partially offset by cryptocurrencies revenue of $120 million, down 55%.
◦ Net interest revenues decreased 9% year-over-year to $415 million , primarily driven by lower securities lending activity and short-term interest rates, partially offset by growth in interest-earning assets.
◦ Other revenues increased 61% year-over-year to $142 million, primarily driven by Trump Account service revenues and increased Robinhood Gold subscription revenues.
• Net income decreased 14% year-over-year to $476 million, and diluted earnings per share ("EPS") decreased 16% to $0.51.
